title: Which digits can p and q be so that 3p7q8 divides by forty four?
description: A five digit number with two missing digits must divide by forty four. Forty four is four times eleven, so the number must pass the test for four and the test for eleven. The test for four lists the choices for q, the test for eleven links p and q, and a check by dividing confirms the pairs.
teaching_notes: One idea: when the divisor is a product of two numbers with no common factor, the number must pass both tests, and each test cuts down the missing digits. Watch for students who test only for eleven, or who let q be any digit because the number ends in eight.

video_script.why: A learner combines the test for four with the excess and short test for eleven to find the missing digits of a number divisible by forty four.
video_script.anchor: the five digit number 3p7q8 with its places marked
video_script.payoff_line: The pairs are seven and zero, five and two, three and four, one and six.

final_answer.spoken: the pairs for p and q are seven and zero, five and two, three and four, one and six

maths_rules: 44 = 4 × 11, and 4 and 11 have no common factor, so the number must pass both tests
test for 4: the last two digits q and 8 must make a multiple of 4: 08, 28, 48, 68, 88, so q is 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8, q even
test for 11: units 8, hundreds 7, ten thousands 3 give excess 8 + 7 + 3 = 18; tens q and thousands p give short p + q
18 − (p + q) is 0 or a multiple of 11; p + q is at most 18, so 18 − (p + q) is 0 or 11, p + q = 18 or 7
p + q = 18 needs p = q = 9, q is odd, and 98 is not a multiple of 4
p + q = 7 with q even: q = 0, p = 7; q = 2, p = 5; q = 4, p = 3; q = 6, p = 1; q = 8 would need p = −1
video_script.design: One idea: use the tests for four and eleven together for forty four. Assumes the test for four and the excess and short test for eleven. The number 3p7q8 stays on the board all video.

beats.on_screen: title card Divisibility by 44; the number 3p7q8 written large with the words divisible by 44 and a question mark

marks.scene: the title card arrives and 3p7q8 is written large
marks.ask: the words divisible by 44? appear under the number

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about a five digit number with two missing digits.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The number is three, p, seven, q, eight. It is divisible by forty four.
Which digits can p and q be?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 44 = 4 × 11 with a tick for the test for 4 and a tick for the test for 11 beside the number 3p7q8

marks.both: two ticks, the test for 4 and the test for 11, appear beside the number

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We use the tests from your book. Forty four is four times eleven.
<bookmark mark='both'/>Four and eleven have no common factor except one. The number must pass the test for four and the test for eleven.

marks.given: the number is written with its digits on their places

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the number three, p, seven, q, eight is divisible by forty four.

beats.on_screen: To find: all pairs of values for p and q

marks.find: the question is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find all the pairs of values for p and q.

beats.on_screen: Test for 4: last two digits q and 8 are 08, 28, 48, 68 or 88, so q is 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8: q is even

marks.last: the last two digits q and 8 are boxed
marks.list: 08, 28, 48, 68 and 88 are written as the multiples of 4
marks.even: q is 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8 is written and tagged even

narration: <bookmark mark='last'/>Step one, use the test for four. The last two digits, which are q and eight, must make a multiple of four.
<bookmark mark='list'/>That happens for zero eight, twenty eight, forty eight, sixty eight and eighty eight.
<bookmark mark='even'/>That gives q as zero, two, four, six or eight. Here q is even.

beats.on_screen: Test for 11: excess 8 + 7 + 3 = 18, short p + q. 18 − (p + q) is 0 or 11, so p + q = 18 or 7

marks.excess: the digits 8, 7 and 3 are picked out and 8 + 7 + 3 = 18 is written
marks.short: the digits q and p are picked out and p + q is written
marks.take: 18 − (p + q) is written, zero or a multiple of 11

narration: <bookmark mark='excess'/>Step two, use the test for eleven. The excess is eight plus seven plus three, which is eighteen.
<bookmark mark='short'/>The short is p plus q.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Eighteen take away p plus q must be zero or a multiple of eleven.
<bookmark mark='two'/>The sum p plus q cannot be more than eighteen. It is eighteen or seven.

beats.on_screen: p + q = 18 needs p = q = 9, q odd, no. p + q = 7 with q even: q = 0, 2, 4, 6 gives p = 7, 5, 3, 1

marks.eighteen: p + q = 18 gives p = q = 9 and is crossed out because 9 is odd
marks.seven: p + q = 7 is written with q even
marks.pairs: q = 0, 2, 4, 6 are written with p = 7, 5, 3, 1 beside them

narration: <bookmark mark='eighteen'/>Step three, join the two tests. Eighteen needs p and q both nine. But q must be even, and nine is odd.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>Take p plus q equal to seven, with q even.
<bookmark mark='pairs'/>If q is zero, p is seven. If q is two, p is five. If q is four, p is three. If q is six, p is one.

marks.back: the four numbers are written with their pairs put back

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step four, put the pairs back and divide by forty four.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Thirty seven thousand seven hundred eight is forty four times eight hundred fifty seven.
<bookmark mark='div2'/>Thirty one thousand seven hundred sixty eight is forty four times seven hundred twenty two.
The other two divide exactly as well.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The pairs are seven and zero, five and two, three and four, one and six.
